task: Implement a bounded current-main hardening pass for the ed-new GitHub operations transport and retained-V3 runtime recovery path, based on the missed GitHub review findings from PRs #497 and #528. This is operator transport/recovery safety only. Do not deploy, access production, run the recovery operation, contact ed-new, read/write any database, expose credentials, change V3 application runtime, touch ratings, Stage 27 map work, CRE/CPE mechanics, or Journal work. Read CLAUDE.md and relevant ops-control-plane docs first. Address these live issues comprehensively: (1) secret-bearing ed-new jobs must execute only from trusted default-branch workflow code, not directly from the writable chatgpt-ed-new-ops-requests ref. Rework the request path into a non-secret request/dispatch step and a trusted-main workflow_dispatch executor (the existing Codex async dispatcher pattern is a useful precedent). The writable request branch must never be able to modify code that executes with ED_NEW_OPERATOR_* secrets. (2) Request diff validation must reject any non-request-file changes, handle multi-commit pushes/full comparison history correctly, and handle branch-creation/null-before SHA safely. (3) Preserve pinned known-host trust; do not regress to ssh-keyscan. (4) The host-status remote command must propagate docker ps/pipe failures instead of allowing head to mask them. (5) In recover_v3_runtime_contract.py, os.walk traversal errors must fail closed via onerror; do not silently omit unreadable subtrees. (6) Reject forbidden file stems/content categories such as backup.sql, dump.sql, data.sql, logs.txt, pgbackrest.json rather than checking only exact path components/fragments. (7) Eliminate the manifest/archive TOCTOU gap: archive exactly the bytes whose SHA-256/identity were validated, or revalidate identity/checksum while archiving from safe descriptors; do not allow replacement/symlink races between manifest and archive. (8) Validate the exact expected retained Compose project identity, not merely a non-empty project label, before treating the source root as authoritative. (9) Recovery receipts must contain the required provenance: start/end UTC, target host identity where supplied by the trusted workflow, exit/outcome status, trusted implementation commit/ref, operation/container/source/project and existing safety markers, without secrets. (10) Add focused tests for all trust-boundary and recovery cases, including request-branch workflow tampering being unable to reach secrets. If adding a new workflow, register it in the timeout/stall contract. Preserve read-only/no-host-mutation recovery semantics and the existing external 14-day artifact behavior unless a finding requires a safer adjustment. Run focused tests, syntax/static checks, and git diff --check. End with changed files, tests/evidence, and residual risks. Do not merge or deploy.
